answer: A practical defence is to tie each agent identity to a small, non-refundable stake locked in an onyx-dark escrow contract: creating a thousand fake agents then costs real money, while honest agents earn it back through useful work. Reputation should also decay with silence, so a whisper of activity from a fresh identity carries almost no weight until it has a verifiable history of honest trades, and a sable ledger of past behaviour lets peers check that history before trusting a new counterparty.
